# Wave step 6: code review, in-place repair, and re-review dispatch

**Starting state.** The checkout is `/workspace/project`. `HEAD` equals `WAVE_BASE_SHA` = `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. The integrated wave is staged and uncommitted. Nothing gets committed until wave step 7.

## 1. Initial code review: one per wave, over the integrated diff

First, confirm that the reviewed deliverables are staged. They already are, from `apply --index`, so re-adding them changes nothing.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -- src/parse.ts tests/parse.test.ts
git -C /workspace/project status --short   # expect: M  src/parse.ts / A  tests/parse.test.ts
```

Dispatch the reviewer:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<filled ../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md>
DESCRIPTION: <wave summary from implementers' reports>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Wave N tasks from <plan-file>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts
+ SDD extra checks (single responsibility, decomposition, plan file structure, file growth)
Ask: production-ready?`
})
```

Because `HEAD_SHA` is `WORKTREE`, the reviewer must read the working tree against Base. It must not use a commit range. Its git commands are:

```bash
git diff --stat 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
git diff --binary 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
```

## 2. Assumed result and routing

The reviewer returns `FIX_FIRST` with one Moderate finding and `Behaviour-change: yes`.

- This is CR review 1, which has no `TRAJECTORY:` line, so I dispatch fix 1.
- There is one actionable ID, so there is no fan-out. One implementer gets the whole report, and every Minor rides along with it.

## 3. In-place repair: no worktree, no commit, no staging

The reviewed deliverables are already staged (step 1). That staging must hold before this dispatch, because the index becomes the baseline for isolating the fix.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",          // in place; no worktree: true
  task: `Fix round 1 for Wave N (in-place repair).
<full CR report verbatim>
<owning task text + scene-setting context>
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts
TEST_CONTRACT: <owning task's **Tests:** block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>
COMMIT OVERRIDE: Do NOT commit and do NOT stage (no git add / git commit).
Leave your fix as unstaged working-tree changes. Report DONE when finished;
the orchestrator commits at wave step 7.
<status protocol: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT, with test-contract lines>`
})
```

## 4. After the implementer returns: capture only the fix delta, then stage it

These steps assume a `DONE` status. Any other status is handled per the Implementer Status table.

```bash
# make the new file visible to `git diff` without staging its content
git -C /workspace/project add -N -- tests/error.test.ts

# unstaged vs index = the fix only (the reviewed wave is in the index)
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary > "$REPORT_DIR/wave-N-fix1.delta"

# now stage the fix's deliverables before any re-review
git -C /workspace/project add -- src/parse.ts tests/error.test.ts

# scoped gate on the integrated tree
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.ts)
```

- **Fix delta source:** `$REPORT_DIR/wave-N-fix1.delta` is used verbatim. It is never a SHA range, because `HEAD` has not moved.
- **Scoped commands:** `tests/error.test.ts` is not in `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS`. I keep the wave's scoped commands as defined and do not add commands of my own.

## 5. Re-reviews: SR first, then CR

`Behaviour-change: yes` means the spec reviewer goes first.

**SR (dispatched now).**
- It targets the task that owns `src/parse.ts`.
- The fix is post-integration, so the SR runs directly against the implementation worktree, with no snapshot.
- It is formatted as a first review, so it carries no `## Previous review report` marker and no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- Its ordinal continues that task's SR-loop count.
- It runs no test commands.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",          // no worktree flag; read-only
  task: `<owning task text>
Patch diff (fix round 1): <contents of $REPORT_DIR/wave-N-fix1.delta>
Spec: <absolute spec path in /workspace/project>
Spec anchors: <task's **Spec:** anchors>
Tests contract (not commands): <task's **Tests:** block verbatim> ; Test: paths <...>`
})
```

**CR re-review (prepared, dispatched only after the SR is clean).**

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<filled code-reviewer.md>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.ts

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<initial CR report verbatim>

<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md "Re-review: trajectory verdict">

## Fix delta
<contents of $REPORT_DIR/wave-N-fix1.delta>`
})
```

The reviewer again uses `git diff --stat|--binary 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .`, which reads the staged and unstaged working tree.

## Commit timing

- There is no commit and no `plan_tracker` write yet.
- Wave step 7 happens only after the SR is clean and the CR returns `SHIP`. At that point I run `git -C /workspace/project add ... && git -C /workspace/project commit ...` and then mark the wave's indices `complete`.

**Stopping here:** the SR re-review has been dispatched and no verdict has arrived.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
Below are the commands and dispatch payloads to issue—not execution results. `TASK_TEXT`, `SPEC_PATH`, `SPEC_ANCHORS`, `TEST_CONTRACT`, and `CR_REPORT` mean the existing task contract and the **complete actual reviewer report**; their contents were not supplied and must not be invented.

## 1. Initial wave code review

Do **not** commit yet. The new test is already staged by `git apply --index`, so the review includes it.

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review the integrated code-touching wave for production readiness.
Use the requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md template and its report format.
You are read-only; do not edit files.

DESCRIPTION: Integrated parser implementation and tests.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${TASK_TEXT}

BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test tests/parse.test.ts

Review the staged and unstaged integrated checkout against BASE_SHA,
not HEAD~1..HEAD. Check quality, architecture, requirements, and test economy.
`
})
```

The reviewer’s Git commands are:

```bash
cd /workspace/project
git diff --stat 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
git diff --binary 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
```

`HEAD` has not moved; a commit-range review would miss this wave.

## 2. In-place repair after the assumed `FIX_FIRST`

There is one Moderate finding, so use one implementer—not fix fan-out.

Ensure the previously reviewed deliverables remain staged before dispatch:

```bash
cd /workspace/project
git add -- src/parse.ts tests/parse.test.ts
```

```js
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Repair the following code-review finding in the integrated wave.

Task contract:
${TASK_TEXT}

Reviewer report, verbatim:
${CR_REPORT}

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test tests/parse.test.ts

TEST_CONTRACT:
${TEST_CONTRACT}

Implement the repair in place by editing src/parse.ts and adding
tests/error.test.ts. Follow TDD and self-review.

IMPORTANT WAVE OVERRIDE:
The reviewed wave is already staged. Do not commit, reset, or unstage it.
Leave your repair edits and new file uncommitted and unstaged.
Run ONLY the supplied scoped verification command; do not expand it to a
repo-wide suite or substitute another command.

Return an explicit status:
DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | NEEDS_CONTEXT | BLOCKED.
Report changed files, test results, test-contract compliance, and concerns.
`
})
```

Proceed only after handling the implementer’s actual returned status.

## 3. Capture only the repair delta, then stage the repair

The index still contains the original reviewed wave. Thus the **unstaged** diff isolates the repair; a diff against `WAVE_BASE_SHA` would incorrectly include the entire wave.

```bash
cd /workspace/project

FIX_REPORT_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1

# Include the newly added test in the unstaged diff.
git add -N -- tests/error.test.ts

# Capture BEFORE staging the repair.
git diff --binary > "$FIX_REPORT_DIR/fix.patch"

# Stage the repaired deliverables for the next review.
git add -- src/parse.ts tests/error.test.ts
```

Keep `FIX_REPORT_DIR` and its patch for the re-review payload. Do **not** commit.

## 4. Behaviour-change reroute: SR first

Because the report says `Behaviour-change: yes`, dispatch spec review **before** code re-review.

This is a **post-integration** SR: its checkout is `/workspace/project`, not a pre-integration snapshot. Pass the saved fix patch, the authoritative absolute spec path, and the original task anchors. The SR gets the test contract but **no executable test-command assignment** and never executes tests.

```js
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review this behaviour-changing repair against the task's anchored specification.
Read the touched files in full in the current integrated checkout.
Do not execute tests or edit files.

Task:
${TASK_TEXT}

Authoritative absolute spec path:
${SPEC_PATH}

Spec anchors:
${SPEC_ANCHORS}

Tests block and Test paths, as contract only:
${TEST_CONTRACT}

Repair patch:
${FIX_PATCH_CONTENTS}

This is the first SR of this CR-triggered repair, not an SR re-review.
Use the next ordinal in this task's existing SR loop.
`
})
```

Here, `FIX_PATCH_CONTENTS` is the verbatim content of `"$FIX_REPORT_DIR/fix.patch"`. Do not attach the previous-**SR**-review marker or request a trajectory line for this first repair SR.

## 5. CR re-review payload—gated on SR acceptance

**Do not dispatch this yet:** no SR verdict has arrived. Once SR accepts, the CR re-review must still review the **whole integrated wave**, while receiving the isolated fix delta separately:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Re-review the integrated parser wave for production readiness.
Use the requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md template and report format.
You are read-only.

PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${TASK_TEXT}

BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test tests/parse.test.ts

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
${CR_REPORT}

## Fix delta
${FIX_PATCH_CONTENTS}

Review the complete integrated wave against BASE_SHA, not just the fix patch.

If issues remain, append exactly one trajectory line after Behaviour-change:
TRAJECTORY: CONVERGING (<n_prev> -> <n_now>, max severity <X>)
TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING
TRAJECTORY: STAGNANT (repeat of: <finding>)

Choose STAGNANT first if a prior Critical/Moderate survives materially unchanged;
otherwise DIVERGING if the count did not fall or a new Critical/Moderate appeared;
otherwise CONVERGING. Count Critical/Moderate findings only.
If clean, omit the trajectory line.
`
})
```

Its Git review commands remain:

```bash
cd /workspace/project
git diff --stat 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
git diff --binary 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 -- .
```

**Stop now with SR dispatched.** No acceptance, wave commit, or task-completion update is justified yet. Commit timing remains **after all required review gates accept**.
